resources.string: FaceScan
Test app with an experimental face surface scan; not a complete 3D head.

On first launch the app downloads about 3.6 MB of model data from Google over HTTPS and verifies it. Google can see your IP address; mobile data charges may apply. Detection does not need a connection afterwards.

Face surface (experimental)

Only the visible front-camera face surface: no hair or back of head. Optional photo texture comes from one view and may include background and shadows. Camera preview and face detection

FaceScan needs camera access for preview and scanning. Face points and the model stay in memory during use. Only if you explicitly choose the photo option is a face photo crop captured in memory and embedded in GLB export. Data is saved only when you explicitly export. You can decline and go back.

Start experimental multi-view scan
Multi-view capture (experimental)

Between captures, turn your head clearly to the left and right, about 15 to 30 degrees each time. Each capture stores the current head pose as its own view. Capture frontal first, add the side views, then reconstruct.

This reconstruction uses a canonical average face as reference. It is not a measurement of your face: shape and scale differ per person and are not validated. It produces an open partial mesh with possible holes, no hair, back of head, photo or animation. No identity check: use one person in one calm session only.

Units and scale follow the canonical average anchors, not your face. The reprojection residual says nothing about real 3D accuracy. Holes, outliers and wrong depth are possible; there is no animation, no photo texture and no completeness guarantee.
